title: Pipecat Cloud: Enterprise Voice Agents Built On Open Source - Kwindla Hultman Kramer, Daily
talk_summary: A Pipecat/Daily co-founder describes building and deploying real-time voice agents: a vendor-neutral open-source pipeline framework plus a thin hosting layer for cold starts, autoscaling, and latency. The actionable content is mostly about model selection tradeoffs (text-mode vs speech-to-speech, Gemini vs GPT pricing) and latency/context effects, not about agent orchestration or software delivery.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep the pipeline vendor-neutral so the same workload can be run against two candidate models and decided by evals rather than opinion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would build a pipecap pipeline and then just swap the two models and run your evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: They note large price gaps between comparable-quality models and let cost drive selection when evals are close.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a 30-minute conversation on Gemini is probably 10 times cheaper than a 30-minute conversation on GPT40
takeaways.numbers: ~10x cheaper for Gemini vs GPT-4o on a 30-minute conversation

takeaways.technique: Keep reasoning in text, not raw multimodal tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue audio tokens massively expand context and degrade model performance versus text-mode reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you're operating in audio mode, you're just sort of expanding the context massively relative to operating in text mode

takeaways.technique: Deploy near inference, minimize round trips
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of many round trips to distant inference, they co-locate compute with inference servers and accept one long hop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just deploy close to the inference servers rather than close to the users and optimize for having one long trip

takeaways.technique: LLM-as-judge as a second pipeline participant
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a second model instance as a judge/participant that inspects the main flow's output in real time and gates routing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's sort of an LLM as a judge pattern here but in the context of a game
